Job Description

Note: Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship for this position.

The Role

Fidelity Charitable is adding a Director, Software Engineering to our Durham regional campus. As a Director, Engineering you'll be responsible for defining and executing the technical strategy for one or more applications aligned with your capability area. You'll partner closely with product managers, architects, IT project managers, systems analysts, and other enabling functions to translate strategic business objectives into scalable, secure, and resilient technology solutions.

In this role, you'll own the end‑to‑end delivery, technical health, and operational stability of your applications and products while you also lead a delivery team of software engineers, systems analysts, and quality testers. You'll balance product‑level priorities with enterprise goals, ensure adherence to standards and best practices, and foster a culture of engineering excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Our technology solutions support the philanthropic community, including donors, financial advisors, and operations professionals, who work together to drive charitable giving through grants to nonprofit organizations.

Define and communicate a clear engineering strategy and execution roadmap aligned with business goals, product vision, and enterprise technology direction
Own delivery targets, ensuring focus on business outcomes, customer experience, and long‑term platform sustainability
Translate business, regulatory, and operational requirements into technical milestones and delivery plans
Apply enterprise thinking to balance near‑term product needs with reuse, scalability, and standardization across the ecosystem
Provide technical leadership across a cross-functional delivery team, ensuring solutions are scalable, secure, and operationally sound
Maintain strong technical credibility with experience across web services and APIs, database systems, modern web architectures, and distributed systems
Partner with architecture and engineering peers to ensure technical quality, maintainability, and architectural integrity
Ensure on‑time, high‑quality releases, while maintaining platform stability during production support, peak periods, and market events
Lead engineering input related to estimation, dependency mapping, sequencing, and capacity planning
Partner with product and program/project Management to ensure delivery health, progress transparency, and stakeholder communication
Champion continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) practices to improve quality, speed, and reliability
Support production incident and outage management, including triage, recovery, root cause analysis, and preventive remediation
Accountable for engineering talent lifecycle: hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, and career development
Build, mentor, and scale high‑performing engineering leadership teams that embrace innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement
Drive adoption of modern engineering practices, tools, and ways of working, leading teams through change effectively

The Expertise And Skills You Bring

Proven software engineering leadership experience
Experience directly managing engineers responsible for full lifecycle delivery, including design, development, testing, deployment, and production support
Experience leading distributed teams, improving team maturity, and enabling teams to think strategically and not simply execute requests
Clear and confident communication skills to explain complex technical topics to a wide range of stakeholders
Ability to influence decisions without direct authority, make sound judgment calls and drive alignment across a complex ecosystem
Comfort operating across the full software development lifecycle, from early requirements through post-release support and incident management
Strong conceptual understanding of object‑oriented design and engineering design patterns
Hands‑on experience designing and delivering RESTful APIs and distributed services
Experience with relational and NoSQL databases
Solid understanding of SDLC best practices, governance, and quality controls
Passion for continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD)

The Team

Fidelity Charitable is a 501(c)(3) public charity. We help donors maximize their generosity through our donor-advised fund, called the Giving Account. Established in 1991, we are the nation’s top grantmaker, distributing $18.3 billion to charities in 2025. Fidelity’s Charitable Technology group develops the next-generation technologies that directly impacts how customers accomplish their philanthropic goals. As a member of the Fidelity Investments business unit supporting Fidelity Charitable and other philanthropic solutions for customers, companies, and financial advisors, you will help our applications evolve through hands-on software development, technical mentoring, and cross-team collaboration with a diverse, co-located engineering team, while also visualizing customer issues as drivers for internal change.

Fidelity’s Onsite Working Model

Fidelity is transitioning to a full-time onsite working model through a phased rollout across regions and roles. Currently, some roles and locations require 100% onsite presence, while others require less. Onsite expectations are likely to evolve as the rollout continues. This transition does not apply to fully remote roles.

jobs.description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

About The Role

We are looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the Identity and Integrations Products team within Security Products. This team builds and operates foundational capabilities for integrations connecting CoreWeave to the breadth of customer security infrastructure, enterprise identity providers and directory services, cloud-native and on-prem key/secrets management (KMS, HSM), and third-party security platforms such as Wiz, CrowdStrike, and SIEM systems.

The role combines people leadership with strong technical judgment: you will guide architecture and engineering decisions, create clarity in complex problem spaces, and ensure that our services meet the availability, security, interoperability, and operational standards expected of a critical cloud platform. You will work closely with product, security, infrastructure, platform, and customer-facing engineering teams.

The ideal candidate has led teams building distributed systems and security-sensitive services and is energized by solving hard problems at the intersection of identity, platform infrastructure, and customer trust.

What You Will Do

Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing Identity and Integrations Products engineering team, including hiring, career development, performance management, and team health.
Set the team’s technical vision, roadmap, priorities, and execution strategy in partnership with Product Managers and Security Products leadership.
Own service reliability and operational excellence, including availability, latency, incident response, change management, capacity planning, and continuous improvement.
Establish engineering practices for secure development, architecture reviews, operational readiness, and sustainable delivery.
Drive effective cross-functional collaboration across security, infrastructure, networking, developer platform, cloud operations, product, and customer engineering teams.
Partner with Product Managers, customer-facing engineering teams and customers to understand integration requirements, guide technical discovery, plan rollouts, and resolve complex integration issues.
Communicate technical decisions, tradeoffs, risks, and progress clearly to engineering, product, security, and executive stakeholders.

What You Bring

5+ years of experience managing a complex function or multiple related teams led by manager / tech-leads, including responsibility for strategy, execution, staffing, and engineering quality.
Experience running engineering operations (observability, SLOs, incident management, post-incident review, capacity planning, release safety) for high-scale services with 99.95%+ availability, 10K RPS or greater.
Demonstrated ability to make sound technical decisions in ambiguous environments and translate long-term strategy into pragmatic execution.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence across organizational boundaries and work with external customers or partners.
A track record of delivering through ambiguity and aligning Product, Engineering, Security, and Infrastructure stakeholders.
Willingness to work on-site in Sunnyvale, California. This role is not remote.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building security products or platforms for enterprise, regulated, or security-sensitive customers.
Experience with identity, key management, encryption, secrets management, confidential computing, or security integrations.
Experience partnering with external customers, technology partners, or security reviewers on product requirements and assurance.
Experience leading greenfield products from early architecture through production adoption.

Build trust with the Identity and Integrations Products team and key partner organizations.
Establish a clear technical and execution roadmap aligned with Security Products and CoreWeave priorities.
Improve the reliability, observability, and operational maturity of the team’s most critical services.
Raise the quality and consistency of architecture, security, and operational reviews.
Hire and develop exceptional engineers while creating a healthy, accountable, and high-performing team culture.

Security Products is building the systems that make CoreWeave trustworthy at scale. You will have the opportunity to lead a team responsible for foundational capabilities that protect access to cloud resources, enable secure product experiences, and support customers running critical AI workloads.

This is a high-impact leadership role for an engineering manager who wants to shape both the technology and the organization behind a modern cloud security platform.

and requires working on-site. Remote work is not available for this role.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering - New Ventures
jobs.description:
Location:
Los Angeles, CA
Work model:
Hybrid, 3–4 days per week onsite

The Opportunity
We are partnering with a healthcare venture-building organization that is creating new technology companies alongside one of the country’s leading healthcare institutions.
The team works directly with clinicians, researchers, and healthcare operators to identify important problems, evaluate where AI can create a meaningful advantage, and test new business concepts through hands-on technical investigation and prototyping.
They are now hiring a Director of Applied AI, New Ventures to help turn early ideas into validated products and investable companies.

This is not a traditional engineering management position. You will operate as a hands-on technical venture builder, moving between product discovery, applied AI, prototyping, technical diligence, and early company creation.

What You’ll Do
Work directly with clinicians, researchers, and operational leaders to uncover meaningful healthcare problems and opportunities.
Translate complex workflows and data into technically grounded product and venture concepts.
Build wireframes, proofs of concept, and early AI-powered prototypes to test the most important assumptions.
Evaluate whether a concept is technically feasible, commercially valuable, and genuinely differentiated.
Assess models, tools, datasets, vendors, and emerging technologies as part of the technical diligence process.
Determine where AI creates a durable advantage and where simpler technology may be more appropriate.
Present technical findings, risks, and recommendations to internal investment stakeholders.
Support funded companies with architecture, data strategy, AI implementation, deployment, scaling, and early technical hiring.
Develop AI-enabled research and evaluation workflows that accelerate market analysis and technical diligence.
Manage several early-stage concepts simultaneously and quickly identify which should progress, change direction, or be discontinued.

You will likely have:
5+ years of experience building technology products, including meaningful work in an early-stage or highly ambiguous environment.
Experience taking a product, company, or major initiative from idea to working prototype or initial launch.
Strong hands-on experience building with modern AI and LLM technologies.
Must have experience using tools such as Claude Code, ChatGPT, or similar AI development environments as part of your everyday workflow.
The ability to prototype using Python and modern product-development tools.
Strong product judgment and the ability to determine which problems are worth solving.
Experience making practical decisions around architecture, data, models, vendors, and build versus buy.
The communication skills to work effectively with clinicians, executives, founders, engineers, and investment stakeholders.
A commercial and entrepreneurial mindset, with an understanding of how technical decisions influence company creation.
Comfort working across multiple ideas without predefined requirements or a traditional product roadmap.

Healthcare experience is valuable but not required. Deep technical ability, product instinct, hands-on building experience, and an authentic interest in improving healthcare are more important.
You May Be a Strong Fit If
You have founded or helped build an early-stage company.
You still enjoy building prototypes yourself, regardless of your current title.
You are naturally curious and quickly identify the few questions that determine whether an idea will work.
You can distinguish a meaningful AI advantage from a superficial feature or wrapper.
You are equally comfortable discussing user problems, business models, data, and technical architecture.
You enjoy working directly with users and domain experts rather than building from predetermined specifications.
You know when to keep exploring an idea and when to stop investing time in it.
Other founders and technical leaders regularly seek your advice on difficult product and engineering decisions.

Why This Role?
This opportunity offers the chance to work at the intersection of applied AI, healthcare, and company creation. Rather than spending several years focused on one product, you will help explore multiple problems, build new concepts, influence investment decisions, and support the creation of companies that could materially improve healthcare delivery.

The position also includes a distinctive long-term incentive tied to a broader portfolio of healthcare ventures, allowing you to participate in value created across multiple companies rather than a single startup.

The Opportunity
We are partnering with a healthcare venture-building organization that is creating new technology companies alongside one of the country’s leading healthcare institutions.
The team works directly with clinicians, researchers, and healthcare operators to identify important problems, evaluate where AI can create a meaningful advantage, and test new business concepts through hands-on technical investigation and prototyping.
They are now hiring a Director of Applied AI, New Ventures to help turn early ideas into validated products and investable companies.

This is not a traditional engineering management position. You will operate as a hands-on technical venture builder, moving between product discovery, applied AI, prototyping, technical diligence, and early company creation.

What You’ll Do
Work directly with clinicians, researchers, and operational leaders to uncover meaningful healthcare problems and opportunities.
Translate complex workflows and data into technically grounded product and venture concepts.
Build wireframes, proofs of concept, and early AI-powered prototypes to test the most important assumptions.
Evaluate whether a concept is technically feasible, commercially valuable, and genuinely differentiated.
Assess models, tools, datasets, vendors, and emerging technologies as part of the technical diligence process.
Determine where AI creates a durable advantage and where simpler technology may be more appropriate.
Present technical findings, risks, and recommendations to internal investment stakeholders.
Support funded companies with architecture, data strategy, AI implementation, deployment, scaling, and early technical hiring.
Develop AI-enabled research and evaluation workflows that accelerate market analysis and technical diligence.
Manage several early-stage concepts simultaneously and quickly identify which should progress, change direction, or be discontinued.

You will likely have:
5+ years of experience building technology products, including meaningful work in an early-stage or highly ambiguous environment.
Experience taking a product, company, or major initiative from idea to working prototype or initial launch.
Strong hands-on experience building with modern AI and LLM technologies.
Must have experience using tools such as Claude Code, ChatGPT, or similar AI development environments as part of your everyday workflow.
The ability to prototype using Python and modern product-development tools.
Strong product judgment and the ability to determine which problems are worth solving.
Experience making practical decisions around architecture, data, models, vendors, and build versus buy.
The communication skills to work effectively with clinicians, executives, founders, engineers, and investment stakeholders.
A commercial and entrepreneurial mindset, with an understanding of how technical decisions influence company creation.
Comfort working across multiple ideas without predefined requirements or a traditional product roadmap.

Healthcare experience is valuable but not required. Deep technical ability, product instinct, hands-on building experience, and an authentic interest in improving healthcare are more important.

You have founded or helped build an early-stage company.
You still enjoy building prototypes yourself, regardless of your current title.
You are naturally curious and quickly identify the few questions that determine whether an idea will work.
You can distinguish a meaningful AI advantage from a superficial feature or wrapper.
You are equally comfortable discussing user problems, business models, data, and technical architecture.
You enjoy working directly with users and domain experts rather than building from predetermined specifications.
You know when to keep exploring an idea and when to stop investing time in it.
Other founders and technical leaders regularly seek your advice on difficult product and engineering decisions.

Why This Role?
This opportunity offers the chance to work at the intersection of applied AI, healthcare, and company creation. Rather than spending several years focused on one product, you will help explore multiple problems, build new concepts, influence investment decisions, and support the creation of companies that could materially improve healthcare delivery.

The position also includes a distinctive long-term incentive tied to a broader portfolio of healthcare ventures, allowing you to participate in value created across multiple companies rather than a single startup.

The products we build are used every day by radiologists making critical decisions with diagnoses that determine what care patients receive next. That’s not a context where “good enough” ships.

We’re looking for a Senior Engineering Manager who can hold that standard while also scaling a team that keeps pace with Rad AI’s growth. Someone who has lived through the full lifecycle of production software from the architectural decision that aged well to the one that didn’t and who brings that hard-won judgment to every conversation with their engineers.

The Corporate Vice President – Enterprise PKI & Cryptographic Engineering is a senior, hands-on technical leader accountable for the architecture, engineering, and modernization of New York Life's enterprise Public Key Infrastructure, certificate lifecycle, and cryptographic services across data center, cloud (AWS, Azure, and GCP), applications, devices, workloads, and non-human identities. This is a builder role, not a purely advisory one: you'll move from architecture into hands-on design, automation, and production delivery.

You'll own PKI and certificate lifecycle automation end to end, serve as the CISO organization's PKI and cryptographic subject matter expert for the Security Review Board and IS Exception process, and help position NYL for cryptographic agility and post-quantum readiness.

What You'll Do

Design, engineer, and modernize enterprise PKI services and trust hierarchies — offline root CAs, issuing/subordinate CAs, and cloud-native issuance — spanning users, applications, devices, workloads, APIs, and non-human identities.
Engineer and administer Microsoft AD CS, including CA configuration, certificate templates, auto-enrollment, trust chains, CRLs, OCSP, and recovery capabilities.
Own Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM): drive discovery, inventory, issuance, renewal, revocation, and reporting from fragmented manual processes toward centralized, policy-driven automation.
Build automation and reusable, self-service certificate APIs using ACME, SCEP, EST, REST, PowerShell, and Python; integrate with ServiceNow, CI/CD, Kubernetes, and DevOps tooling.
Engineer HSM/KMS backed CA and signing services, including key ceremonies, backup, rotation, access control, and disaster recovery, across on-prem and cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP).
Serve as the PKI and cryptographic engineering subject-matter expert for the Security Review Board and Architecture Review Board, and provide authoritative technical risk recommendations on IS Exception requests.
Maintain strong knowledge of Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID where they intersect with certificate services, certificate-based authentication, device identity, Conditional Access, and Privileged Identity Management.
Maintain the enterprise cryptographic inventory and drive cryptographic agility, short-lived certificates, and post-quantum migration readiness.
Treat PKI as business critical infrastructure: define resiliency, monitoring, and recovery procedures, and lead incident response and root-cause analysis for certificate, key, and trust failures.
Serve as the senior technical authority for complex production certificate, trust, and cryptographic issues, translating decisions into reusable enterprise patterns.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years of progressive, hands-on experience in PKI, cryptographic engineering, identity engineering, or security engineering, with significant responsibility for enterprise PKI environments.
Deep hands-on experience engineering or operating enterprise certificate authority environments, including Microsoft AD CS, certificate templates, trust chains, CRLs, and OCSP.
Strong understanding of X.509, TLS/mTLS, certificate enrollment, revocation, trust models, and cryptographic key management.
Experience implementing or operating an enterprise CLM platform and automating certificate lifecycle processes with ACME, SCEP, EST, REST APIs, PowerShell, or Python.
Experience with certificate discovery and inventory across complex enterprise infrastructure, cloud platforms, containers, and Kubernetes.
Experience with HSMs, KMS platforms, private-key protection, or cloud key-management services.
Experience integrating PKI with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), APIs, DevOps pipelines, service meshes, and workload identity patterns.
Strong knowledge of Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID, particularly where they intersect with PKI, certificate-based authentication, device identity, or non-human identity.
Ability to conduct deep technical security reviews, identify material PKI and cryptographic risks, and define practical remediation or compensating controls.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex PKI and cryptographic risk to engineers, architects, governance bodies, auditors, vendors, and senior leaders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with enterprise CLM platforms such as Venafi, AppViewX, Keyfactor, or DigiCert Trust Lifecycle Manager.
Experience modernizing Microsoft AD CS or migrating toward managed private CA or PKI-as-a-Service.
Experience with cloud PKI technologies such as AWS Private CA, Google Cloud Certificate Authority Service, or Azure Key Vault/Cloud PKI.
Experience integrating certificate lifecycle capabilities with ServiceNow or similar workflow platforms.
Experience with code signing, S/MIME, device certificates, Kubernetes certificate management, or service-mesh mTLS.
Experience with cryptographic inventory, cryptographic-agility programs, or post-quantum migration initiatives.
Experience implementing Microsoft's Enterprise Access Model, Tier 0 protections, or privileged-access modernization.
Prior experience supporting a Security Review Board, Architecture Review Board, or IS Exception process; financial services or other regulated enterprise experience; relevant certifications (CISSP, CISM, CCSP, or a cloud security credential).
